Attention mechanisms are widely used in neural machine translation to
address the sequence-to-sequence problem's challenge. However, most studies are
limited to theoretical evaluations and lack practical application. Our research
aims to bridge this gap by being among the first to assess attention's efficacy
in a real-world neural machine translation scenario. Our findings indicate that
production efficiency can be significantly enhanced by training the encoder and
translator models independently before integrating them with attention
mechanisms. Our proposed look-forward attention mechanism outperforms existing
approaches, yielding a 2.5-fold increase in production speed with comparable
output quality. Our results are documented for multiple language pairs including
English-to-Monk's Nonsense Language, English-to-German, and WMT's English-to-Spanish.
Our production metrics are available on our website at https://github.com/parhamsh/look-forward.

This study offers an educational translation case for researchers and practitioners in computing, using a translational method to identify key achievements in the development of grid computing. By applying this method, the research team defined the success criteria for grid computing projects, which needed to be globally accessible applications capable of significant power consumption reductions. According to the translational method's phase framework, the research team has defined essential translation enablers for grid computing within each of the four framework phases. These enablers are supported by specific research areas and technological advancements depicted in a comprehensive roadmap.

A new dark matter paradigm, known as the Combined Dark Fluid, has emerged with the concept of dark matter and dark energy being fundamentally connected. Based on the dissipative fluid theory, this confluence implies that dark matter inherently exhibits dissipation at a fundamental level. To explore the characteristics of the dissipative Combined Dark Fluid, we derived its field equations and analyzed structural properties, including equilibrium and force densities. Simulating a simulated galaxy, we found that the model can be successfully described under certain conditions, indicating its ability to address some key challenges of dark matter models.

In the realm of education, fostering curiosity is of paramount importance to effectively engage learners. Nevertheless, measuring curiosity within educational settings remains a significant challenge. Our research aims to tackle this issue by examining how to assess curiosity within collaborative learning environments. Our proposed framework introduces a set of metrics that can gauge curiosity levels in real-time among learners working together on projects. By analyzing verbal and non-verbal communication, our pilot study successfully demonstrated accurate curiosity level predictions. Moreover, the data collected from this study was made openly available to other researchers for further investigation and replication.

Moving beyond a Gaussian covariance model called a Mat\'ern function to graphically correlated data, we've developed a new approach for specifying dependencies. This method provides a flexible graph-based correlation model that can capture a wide range of data interactions. The development of an efficient inverse Cholesky factor for the Mat\'ern precision matrix enables rapid and accurate parameter estimation through marginal likelihood evaluation. Our efficient fitting procedure is showcased in contrast to existing methods for predicting continuous outcomes, which we compare against in practical tests, including how a model using a specific graph performed when trying to predict the water content of trees.

The effectiveness of using mobile data from mobile phones for estimating travel times and identifying missing road segments relies on strategically selecting missing segments. Some previous studies have focused on mobile data quality but neglected the choice of missing segments, while others attempted to optimize data quality but ignored connectivity. This work aims to identify missing road segments that maximize data connectivity, allowing for better detection of the urban road system. A method is proposed to identify missing road segments that allow for robust connectivity of a large number of ridesharing vehicles, and it is proven mathematically that this method can achieve optimal system-wide connectivity. Characteristics of mobile data from mobile phones are analyzed to develop a framework for urban road system detection, and an algorithm is proposed to efficiently implement this system. Numerical experiments demonstrate the proposed method's ability to successfully identify a large portion of the urban road system with large numbers of mobile data sources. Additionally, characteristics of mobile data from mobile phones are analyzed to develop a method for detecting urban road systems using mobile data from mobile phones.

We delve into the $J/\psi\to (\gamma + ){\rm invisible}$ decay, which we express in terms of neutrino field interactions within the effective field theory framework, Higgs effective field theory, and massive gluon effective field theory. Each framework offers unique insights, with implications for neutrino properties, quantum gravity, and cosmology, including potential links to the Lorentz symmetry breaking observed in neutrino experiments, the residual presence of relic gravitational waves, and the nature of dark matter. Notably, the study of $J/\psi\to (\gamma + ){\rm invisible}$ decay and the associated data can provide valuable information about extremely light neutrinos, the massive gluon effective field theory can be developed systematically via the construction of the Lagrangian, with implications for the decay rate that are within the range of experimental detection, with a predicted range of $0.4$ to $1.8$ femtobarns, considering the validity of the effective field theories.

Recently, standard differential equations have gained significant attention due to their precise modeling of1T1-transmons in superconducting quantum circuits, ultimately enabling enhanced efficiency of quantum computations. These differential equations, which include negative exponentials and indicial singularities at specific time points representing events such as pulsing and measurement, traditionally require numerical solutions. Nonetheless, existing integration methods struggle to maintain stability and accuracy, particularly when dealing with impulse functions. In response to this challenge, our proposal involves the development of an implicit variable stepsize multistep method tailored for the direct integration of standard differential equations. Initially, we examine the impact of standard differential equations on the efficiency of gate operations and identify their potential implications. Subsequently, we evaluate the proposed method's performance through theoretical convergence analysis, error constant computation, and extensive testing on stepsize control. Findings suggest that our approach offers competitive A-stability, precise predictions of local truncation errors, and more stable and accurate results compared to previous methods, ultimately resulting in improved overall performance.

Analyzing large-scale, multivariate time series data that vary across different dimensions is crucial in fields such as econometrics, engineering, and the natural sciences. Although the data's complex structure provides significant insights, it also poses processing challenges. To tackle this, researchers have developed various techniques to simplify and break down the data, including Multivariate Adaptive Spectral Regression, Singular Spectrum Analysis, and Fourier transformation. This paper examines the properties of consistent and rate-optimal multivariate functional SSA methods for converting complex data into a more manageable one-dimensional time series format, and demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a multivariate functional SSA application.

Auto-explainable AI (AXAI) is an emerging field aiming to provide comprehensible and trustworthy machine learning predictions. However, recent studies have identified inaccuracies in certain AXAI methods, primarily attributed to their incorrect attribution of output variations. This article delves into the root causes of this issue, identifying three distinct factors: (1) inherent complexity, (2) inherent obscurity, and (3) insufficient capacity. In response, we examine a broader class of AXAI methods, including posthoc interpreters, counterfactuals, and natural language explanations, and propose addressing these limitations through (1) capacity augmentation, and (2) risk mitigation frameworks. Our research suggests that most current AXAI models exhibit excessive stability and heightened responsiveness to minor perturbations. To validate these claims, we conducted a thorough analysis involving a broad array of models, including decision trees, random forests, neural networks, linear regression, and linear models, across multiple scenarios. Our proposed capacity augmentation framework consists of five components addressing missing aspects in most AXAI methods. To mitigate the risks associated with AXAI methods, we suggest a unified risk assessment consisting of reliability, robustness, and risk control. Lastly, we discuss the theoretical aspects of these concepts and their relevance to real-world applications.

The one-dimensional random walk is notorious for recurring infinitely in an infinite time span, yet it also has an infinite probability of staying stationary within a finite range for an infinite duration. To study this phenomenon, we will examine the one-dimensional random walk proceeding along the real line and observe the probability of it not returning to zero at time n+1, given that it remains stationary at or before time n. This investigation will delve into the behavior of this probability for large values of n, considering the underlying mechanism of the random walk.

This research paper detailizes the plasma characteristics and verification procedures of a new operational mode, specifically the helicon mode, in the IShTAR plasma generator. IShTAR, a 0.55-meter radius, 1.5-meter length lower hybrid frequency plasma tool, currently uses a matchbox type plasma generator whose current configuration limits efficient high-power operation due to its LHC frequency. To overcome this limitation, the new matchbox generator will be modified to support the TE11 mode, enabling better high-power performance. Initially, plasma analysis was conducted with ICP-powered original generator before the modification. A theoretical model was then developed to verify the plasma conditions, confirming the accuracy of the model and setting the stage for successful implementation of the helicon mode after the generator modification.

To mitigate biopesticide's susceptibility to microbial mortality, a suppression mechanism was integrated into a biopesticide mathematical model of mutual dependence between microbe and plant, and its impact on biopesticide's reduction in microbial death rate was simulated, and the resulting devaluation of biopesticide's selling price was modeled, and the resulting loss in revenue was determined.

A histopathology image analysis task is complicated due to a vast disparity between the number of background areas and the areas of interest within the images. In practice, this leads to a significant decrease in performance for nucleus segmentation models, particularly in regions with a high density of nuclei. To mitigate this issue, research on nucleus identification in pathology images is focused on developing efficient methods for creating high-quality data sets and devising effective learning algorithms that take into account the imbalance of nucleus and background data. To address these issues in research on image analysis, we propose a novel approach to nucleus identification in histopathology images, which includes a two-stage network called W-Net. This algorithm is built upon the foundation of a U-shape convolutional network and is designed to extract a wide range of features from low to high levels of abstraction, as well as employ an efficient data augmentation technique to minimize model bias towards nucleus and background areas, and enhance the robustness of the model against nuclei-dense regions. The performance of W-Net is evaluated and compared to other leading models in terms of precision, recall, F1 score, and dice coefficient on public data sets, including the PANDA data set and the UCIR data set. Experimental evidence shows that W-Net outperforms other state-of-the-art models, outdoing them by up to 10% in terms of dice coefficient in average across multiple test cases.

We establish a novel result for a specific class of representations of a variety of algebraic groups, namely those that are complementary and regional in nature. These representations, belonging to a family of special orthogonal or symplectic groups of differing characteristics, are shown to accurately determine the underlying group itself, a result that constitutes an inaugural result for a category of representations that are both odd and regional in nature. A distinguishing feature of our approach is the incorporation of a critical element in the process of proving this result that is not often seen in analogous theorems for their general counterparts.

This research paper defines two graph properties - graph D-hamiltonicity and graph D-hamiltonian pathability - in relation to a particular subclass of graphs that are homeomorphic to large-scale simple graphs, denoted as D. We establish sufficient conditions for connected graphs to possess D-hamiltonicity or D-hamiltonian pathability, including correlations with specific properties of their underlying graphs D. Notable results are obtained, such as detecting the line graph L^n(G) hamiltonicity for^n >= 2when G possesses certain connectivity and minimum degree requirements, as well as solving an open problem posed by Bondy and Xu regarding the D-hamiltonicity of (k-1)-tangled graphs forgiven specific examples of graphs that are homeomorphic toand their pathability for a particular set of tangled graphsand their implications on the connectivity and minimum degree of the original graph Gfor its repeated graphsnand their line graphsn, denoted asL^n(G).

Although the mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2-induced pyroptosis are not fully understood, evidence points to the cell's lytic death as a critical event in the pandemic's progression. Pyroptosis, triggered by the release of inflammatory cytokines, can attract crowds and exacerbate symptoms of respiratory distress syndrome. This research explores the cell death dynamics of pyroptosis by utilizing a solitary-cell mathematical model, based on key indicators of cell protein interactions and inflammatory cytokine releases. Our model confirms pyroptotic cell death and examines respiratory distress syndrome's progression via numerical simulations. Notably, treatments targeting TNF$\alpha$ and IL-1$\beta$ release are shown to avert cell death and respiratory distress syndrome in our study's findings.

External influences on an agent's dynamics, such as unobserved state variables, can hinder learning. To understand this learning process, an Markov Decision Process (Mdp) is modeled with these unobserved variables, but an effective policy depends on eliminating them. Previously developed multi-task approaches learn multiple related Mdp instances, but this is inefficient due to the unobserved variables appearing in each instance. We propose a novel framework that models unobserved variables as variables external to the state, determining an additional dynamics component and potentially the reward the agent receives. This approach enables the use of efficient techniques to solve this problem. We characterize the conditions that make this problem solvable and prove that, in certain conditions, it is equivalent to a set of independent Mdp problems. This characterization leads to methods to represent this external environment, and we provide algorithms that transform the original problem into (1) a collection of independent Mdp problems or (2) an Mdp problem with modified reward. We analyze the impact of unobserved external variables on policy optimization, demonstrating how certain variables cannot be ignored, and others are only important for comparing specific alternatives. This understanding guides algorithm design, and we provide theoretical efficiency bounds that guide the development of algorithms. In experiments on tabular problems and a robotic task, we demonstrate the value of identifying and removing unobserved external variables.

The consensus mechanism utilized in blockchain technology necessitates the development of reliable and correct software to prevent fraudulent alterations of transaction data, a challenge addressed by the use of functional programming languages and type systems with static verification. This approach enables the pre-validation of code before deployment, a significant advantage in blockchain technology where code modification is costly and time-consuming. To facilitate this validation, a type checker based on the Coq proof assistant has been created for smart contracts in the Tezos blockchain's smart language, Faustez. This tool ensures the type safety and memory management (GC-safety) of transactions written in the language, a achievement made possible by a rigorous mapping between Garbage Collected Haskell and a core lambda calculus.

Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs) are commonly employed to integrate and analyze non-Euclidean data within the fields of computer vision and signal processing. GCNNs are typically built utilizing graph convolutional layers that leverage graph spectral properties to engage with input data. A graph spectral filter is implicitly created within each GCNN's convolutional layer, which is equivalent to modifying a GCNN for achieving optimal coefficients in a matching filter criterion. This equivalence reveals crucial insights into various GCNN components, including its polynomial behavior, graph spectral elements, and forward propagation dynamics, while also facilitating a more coherent and unified perspective on GCNNs from a signal processing standpoint.

In a model uniting gravity and scalar fields described by Poincar\'e symmetry, a Chern-Simons-like action is developed, resulting in equations identical to those of the primary theory. Implementing specific gauge forces via ansatz, we obtain descriptions of complex, hair-covered black holes and field-dressed solitons. Specifically, we analyze their thermodynamic and gravitational potential properties. Notably, in the case of black holes, a minimum mass threshold, characteristic of the horizon's shape, is identified. Furthermore, in contrast to models incorporating a cosmological constant, there exists in this scenario a repulsive force, associated with flat spacetime, impeding long-range scalar field propagation.

A profound connection between membrane formulations and non-transitive symmetry has been explored, focusing on isotropy in non-commutative spaces. A particular case, involving two-dimensional gauge theories on a 4-sphere, has led to a groundbreaking finding - an equivalence between a Wess-Zumino-Witten theory and a Gauged Nf-point sigma model, with the latter exhibiting non-transitive SL(2,C) symmetry. Notably, this equivalence arises from a membrane that spans a 5-sphere, and it suggests a deeper relationship between these models in higher-dimensional spheres as well. A non-transitive SL(2,C) symmetry has been identified in a particular gauge theory on odd-dimensional spheres as well. A particular membrane has been shown to exhibit this symmetry, and eliminating it results in a non-transitive SL(2,C) symmetry in a gauge theory on a higher-dimensional sphere. A membrane has been found that relates two SL(2,C) symmetric theories on spheres of different dimensions, and further, a membrane has been identified that relates two SL(2,C) symmetric Wess-Zumino-Witten theories with different group structures. A particular supermembrane has been shown to relate two supersymmetric Wess-Zumino-Witten theories and has been used to construct a non-transitive supersymmetric SL(2,C) symmetry in a gauge theory on an odd-dimensional sphere. A particular supermembrane has been found that relates a supersymmetric Wess-Zumino-Witten

In Traditional CSA-based methods, the accuracy of lateral displacement estimation is constrained by the limited number of sampling points, resulting in low spatial resolution. To address this issue, a novel technique called Virtual Origin CSA (VOCSA) is presented, where a synthetic array of signals is generated at closely spaced points along the CSA line by utilizing data from adjacent CSA lines. A case control study was conducted to evaluate the performance of VOCSA in comparison to Traditional CSA, where a simulated tissue phantom with embedded cylindrical structures of varying lateral displacements was utilized as the assessment medium. Displacement estimation was performed using both VOCSA and Traditional CSA methods with a matched filter, and the resulting lateral resolution was determined by the -6dB criterion. Results indicated that VOCSA achieved a lateral resolution approximately four times better than Traditional CSA and maintained nearly identical bias and standard deviation of estimation errors. In conclusion, the VOCSA method significantly enhances the precision of lateral displacement estimation in ultrasound elastography, and its improved lateral resolution makes it a valuable approach for the design of advanced computational models.

Algorithms and corresponding pseudocode are intrinsically linked, as the latter provides the former a clear and usable representation, making it easier for humans to comprehend and execute on computers. Despite this connection, current neural methods for teaching algorithms through video demonstrations and feedback struggle with accurately parsing pseudocode due to the complexity of the syntax. This paper introduces a straightforward and effective neural model called Rational Pseudocode, which connects algorithms with demonstrations by utilizing the structured nature of context-free grammar through a loss function, outperforming the baseline model in experiments conducted on three datasets comprising four algorithms including sorting, shortest path, and game playing, as evidenced by improved pseudocode prediction performance and user study results indicating enhanced readability and algorithm accuracy.

We extend the concept of Boolean Ramsey theory to include posets, specifically $V$-shaped posets within Boolean algebras of height $k$. Our work demonstrates that as the Boolean algebra size $n$ grows without bound, $k$-point Boolean algebras always contain $V$, and we identify the smallest height $k$ where this is true. Additionally, for each Boolean algebra of height $k \ge 3$, we can find an embedding of a specific $V$-shaped poset consisting of antichains of lengths $2$ and $3$.

In recent years, time series data has played a crucial role in various industry sectors and academic fields, with the need for effective methods to analyze such data escalating across multiple markets. Time series data often contains hidden patterns that can provide valuable insights into the underlying distributions, facilitating crucial decisions in fields such as trading and healthcare. However, extracting meaningful information from such data poses significant challenges due to its inherent volume, velocity, and velocity. Effective clustering techniques have proven to be a powerful tool in revealing these underlying structures, thus facilitating more informed decision-making. In this study, we introduce a novel dynamic $k$-means framework, KDM, designed to address the complexities of clustering high-dimensional, unstructured data, such as text data. Our framework integrates innovative techniques, including $k$-means plus-$+$, $k$-means-scan, and the removal of outliers, to effectively manage the dynamic nature of data streams, ensuring efficient and accurate clustering. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the superior performance of KDM in terms of both computational efficiency and accuracy, outperforming existing methods in handling the processing of data and the accuracy of the clusters formed. KDM exhibits the potential to form clusters that are nearly optimal in quality, effectively managing the complexities of high-dimensional, unstructured data in real-time. KDM operates with a temporal complexity of $O(\dim(\mathbf{x})\log (\dim(\mathbf{x})))$ per update, enabling efficient processing of data updates within the established dimension

In the dynamic, hierarchical networks that govern many natural systems, we've developed a novel variation of stochastic pursuit-evasion games by incorporating hierarchical structures into the settings of these competitions. Considerating the relationships between entities and their surrounding environments, we've modified traditional game rules to reflect these multi-level interactions. To illustrate our concepts, we've utilized both numerical examples and theoretical analyses based on 2x2 games, revealing the influence of environmental factors, hierarchical connections, and higher-level competitions on outcomes such as game values, optimal strategies, and distribution patterns. Our research provides a foundation for understanding and addressing complex, hierarchical pursuits-evasion scenarios found in nature.

The concept of circular transitivity, which implies that if entity A is more likely than B, and B is more likely than C, then A is more likely than C, when considering all possible entities, represents a fundamental property. Our study identifies the statistical relationship between entropies and probabilities, thereby expressing circular transitivity in terms of circularly ordered information or uncertainty measures. This enables the classification of entropy-based relationships into linear, circular, or no specific order. A byproduct of our research provides a classification of nontransitive dice, including examples of circular transitivity.

Recently, deep learning techniques have gained popularity in low-dose CT image reconstruction due to their impressive performance, particularly when using end-to-end models. These models, developed through collaborative training of generator and aggregator networks, eliminate the need for the generator to minimize squared errors with respect to paired images. However, prolonged training of such models can lead to overfitting. Our research reveals through experimentation that the generator alone can effectively denoise LD images when employing certain architectures and loss functions, rendering the collaborative model redundant. Building upon this finding, our approach utilizes an AdaSwitch network, which combines multiple denoising networks and selectively selects or removes them based on the dose and optimizes their numbers using AdaOpt. Our model requires no training for the aggregator network and prevents information loss from the HD reference image. AdaSwitch and AdaOpt require no manual parameter tuning, as they adjust network depth according to dose and number of branches, respectively. Our evaluation using the fourfold LSCT dataset demonstrates the efficacy of AdaSwitch and AdaOpt in denosing LD images, as measured by PSNR, SSIM, and LCE metrics.

Recent advancements in dialogue understanding have heavily relied on pre-training models using large-scale, annotated datasets, but this approach is hindered by the scarcity of such data. In this work, we introduce SPACE-2, a novel dialogue pre-training framework that effectively combines two strategies: contrastive learning with unlabeled data and supervised classification with labeled data. To address the challenge of computing contrastive losses between related utterances in data pairs, we introduce a data augmentation technique known as Task Perturbation, and subsequently train encoder components using the computed contrastive losses. To integrate labeled data, we propose a hierarchical structure called Tree-Structured Multi-Task Contrastive Pre-training, which allows for the effective use of datasets with varying annotation densities. Our experiments demonstrate that our method yields significant improvements over existing techniques on three dialogue tasks across two datasets, even when using sparsely annotated data.

This research investigates a perfect fluid cosmological model under specific conditions. 
We establish the relationship between a conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton and a conformal Yamabe-Ricci soliton, and derive a conserved potential function equation. 
Furthermore, we derive a conserved potential function equation and demonstrate that the mean curvature function satisfies an Laplace equation. 
However, if the soliton is expanding, we find that the mean curvature function is constant and thus the soliton is classified as an R-Y(s) soliton. 
We also obtain that the spacetime manifold conformally maps to a Yamabe soliton if the soliton is of the Yamabe type with a Yamabe soliton value of -1/4. 
We then study the relationship between a conformal Ricci-Yamabe soluton and an Yamabe soliton by comparing their curvature functions and establish that the soliton is shrinking if it is of the Yamabe type. 
Finally, we prove that if the soliton is of the Yamabe type and has a constant Yamabe soliton value, it must have a constant Yamabe soliton value of -1/4.

Our proposed BasicVSR++ architecture surpasses the performance of the original BasicVSR model by significantly refining its video super-resolution results. We achieved this improvement by incorporating long-frame propagation and a deformation convolution-based alignment strategy into BasicVSR, drawing from the successful elements of BasicVR and other top-tier methods. Furthermore, we bypassed the limitation imposed by the propagation step's input depth, strategically selecting the frame sequence to maximize the 3-D convolutional network's performance. These innovative techniques enabled BasicVSR++ to effectively integrate information from a wider range of reference frames, resulting in more accurate pixel-level data flow and the extraction of more comprehensive information. These advancements contributed to the overall video super-resolution performance, yielding visible gains over the original BasicVSR model.

The pursuit of generalizable intelligent agents through model-based multi-task learning has been hindered by the exponential growth of parameters when combining learned components. In contrast to this limitation, our research indicates that an infinite number of distinct but related learning tasks can be achieved even with a finite number of parameters, by employing an innovative approach that isolates parameters into independent, non-interfering subsets, or 'modules'. Each module is responsible for a specific task, or a closely related subset of tasks, and we define and analyze an agent composed of these modules, an n-module system, within the framework of the Dynamic Decision Network (DDN). Theoretical analysis reveals, in the context of DDNs, that each module's parameters remain unaffected by the presence of additional modules, and further, that an infinite number of distinct but related learning tasks can be achieved by simply adding or removing modules. The finiteness of shared parameters within each module accelerates the data efficiency of an n-module system by allowing it to leverage existing parameter knowledge from previous tasks with overlapping sets of parameters. The theoretical findings are validated by the successful application of an optimal 2-module DDN system and a data-efficient 4-module DDN system on a complex multi-task visual navigation benchmark. The designed systems exhibit notable performance, consistently surpassing single-task systems and frequently outperforming non-modular systems.

The construction of discrete approximations for the porous medium equation and its variant on a complete, non-compact metric measure space with a compact boundary is examined. Using discrete analogues of key identities from the continuous setting, including a Caccioppoli-type identity, energy dissipation identity, and Bochner-type formula, estimates for the approximate solutions are obtained. Certain regularity and compactness properties are also demonstrated for the approximate solutions, with a compactness argument ultimately yielding the existence of solution semigroups for both the porous medium equation and its modified form.

In 1943, Godel proved his incompleteness theorems, revealing the existence of an unprovably true statement within any consistent extension of Peano Arithmetic (PA). In 1945, Tarski discovered his truth definition theorem, which provided an undecidable definition of true sentences in the language of PA. Subsequently, Carnap applied modal operators to create complete modal extensions of PA, although his method relied on the assumption of consistency. In 1947, Rosser enhanced PA with an uncompletable conservative extension, based on diagonalization.

In Clifford analysis, an operator T analogous to the Cauchy-Riemann operator exists, with its eigenfunctions representing harmonic functions due to the coincidence of operators T and T_bar. Due to the infinite dimensionality of its constituent parts, both operators share the same Dirichlet problem solutions and eigenfunction representations. For any three non-overlapping spheres within R^n+, there exists a function f that is T-eigen可展 and equals -1 on the boundaries of these spheres, specifically being the unique solution to a constrained optimization problem defined by a given norm on a three-sphere boundary. The solution's equality holds for common norms such as L^1, L^2, and the infinity norm. The concept of T-eigen可展 functions being intrinsically linked to the Poisson kernel, which in turn relates to the Dirichlet kernel, constitutes the foundation of this theoretical framework.

This paper introduces a novel approach called Sequential Geographically Balanced Sampling (SeGBS) to efficiently select a balanced sample from the population within a specified region. 
As opposed to traditional methods, SeGBS allows for sampling from the population that is not available on a media format and is instead accessible as a sequence of units in a time series. 
The sequence should ideally contain information about the geographic location of each unit. 
Geographic balancing is achieved by assigning weights to a geospatial hash of each unit's location and selecting a balanced sample based on the minimum distance rule. 
The introduction of the sequential nature allows for cost-effective field data collection and increases flexibility in survey design. 
Two case studies are used to evaluate the accuracy and geographic distribution of the estimates produced by SeGBS and compare it to other sampling methods such as Simple Random Sampling and Geographically Balanced Sampling. 
The findings indicate that SeGBS yields comparable accuracy and geographic distribution of the estimates to Geographically Balanced Sampling but with less computational efficiency and increased estimation bias.

Robot arm calibration using an attached camera is essential for accurate task execution. Typically, extracalibration of the camera requires expert assistance and precise equipment to track both the robot's position and the camera's orientation. However, these methods are not accessible to users of everyday robot systems. Relying on deep learning techniques to identify object locations and orientations from images, despite being a common approach, comes with significant concerns about reliability, security, and consistency. We present a novel method that learns to adjust the robot's positioning and the camera's calibration based on images, utilizing just one type of reference object. This method allows a robot to accurately identify and locate standard objects from images by adjusting its position and the camera's calibration based on pre-trained facts, rather than depending on the object detection model's output. This method is easy to understand, transparent, and requires no additional training data for the object detection model. We demonstrate the method's effectiveness by showing how it can correctly identify objects in images with as little as 10% of the expected error margin.

High-resolution solution estimation in image restoration is a critical component of image recovery processes. In image recovery, extracting the conditional posterior distribution is an essential extraction post processing step that allows for the selection of a specific posterior image, typically the one with the highest probability density. This extraction is usually triggered by regulations imposed by external factors, such as gauge invariance in positron emission tomography (PET) or the lack of measurement preservation in tomographic synthesis problems. However, current methods for extracting the posterior in PET and tomographic synthesis, which are based on Markov chain Monte Carlo techniques, often struggle to generate preserved measurement samples due to their iterative nature and may fail when the prior is highly influential, as is the case with deep learning-based tomographic images that aim to recover high-resolution images. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative technique utilizing generative adversarial networks in conjunction with Monte Carlo sampling to accelerate the extraction process and ensure preserved measurement samples, even when the prior is constrained. The introduced method involves training two sets of regularized conditional and non-conditional generative models and integrating Monte Carlo sampling with their training to control the posterior distribution, thus enabling efficient extraction. The advantages of this technique are demonstrated in PET and tomographic synthesis data completion tasks.

This note addresses the issue of invariant solutions in dynamical systems characterized by fractional order. We begin by offering a definition of invariant surfaces and then prove that certain defined surfaces cannot serve as invariant surfaces in these types of systems. Additionally, we examine a specific system with two previously reported invariant surfaces of a lower order, however, a closer analysis reveals these surfaces are not truly invariant.

Next-generation wireless networks will utilize terahertz frequencies to significantly boost data transfer speeds over short distances, yet signal degradation over those distances demands the implementation of multi-hop beam training procedures. This paper addresses the beam training challenge by presenting a novel joint single-device and multi-device approach that minimizes beam training latency and reduces energy consumption. This innovative method leverages reinforcement learning techniques to streamline the beam training process, simultaneously determining optimal beams for both single and multi-device scenarios. Simulations demonstrate the superior performance of this approach by achieving a 20% reduction in training latency and beam search depth in comparison to conventional exhaustive beam training procedures.

Located in the Scorpius-Centaurus stellar association, the L14, the Earth's ionosphere can be studied by analyzing the scintillation of the radio waves from the pulsar B1333+16 as they pass through this bright luminosity. By correlating long-term observations of the scintillation patterns with optical data, researchers have been able to map out the properties of electron-rich clouds in the interstellar space. The rate of change in the path length of the scintillation patterns is related to relative movements between the Earth and the pulsar, as well as movements within the Local Group. The analysis of these movements indicates that the clouds are moving away from us at a rate of about 40-70 kilometers per million light years, which is consistent with the expansion of the universe. Furthermore, the shape of the clouds appears to be rotating counterclockwise, likely due to the spin of nearby neutron stars and other compact stellar objects.

This paper presents a generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPWaveNet) to enhance the diversity of speech generated by deep learning-based text-to-speech systems. QPWaveNet, which builds upon the QPSTM quality text-to-speech synthesis, is a type of autoregressive model that is structured using a dilated convolution neural network. QPWaveNet is the first example of a QPSTM-based model to operate on raw waveforms. QPWaveNet is distinguished by the use of quasi-periodic units in place of the standard QPSTM units. The QPSTM's characteristics of quality control and style transfer are maintained by QPWaveNet. We refer to QPWaveNet's characteristics of quasi-periodicity and quality as its QP-Q. We have conducted experiments on the JVS and LJ samples. The results reveal that QPWaveNet demonstrates superior performance over QPSTM in terms of naturalness and timbre. Moreover, QPWaveNet's synthesis capabilities are verified, and the use of QPWaveNet as an encoder to train a QPSTM decoder has been demonstrated. The results show the DEC-QPSTM's performance is significantly superior to the original QPSTM model. The DEC-QPSTM model also exhibits improved timbre. The QPWaveNet model's equations, network structure, and implementation details are provided to the research community.

This research presents a novel, accessible web platform called MADARi, designed to facilitate efficient annotation of detailed Arabic word annotations and simultaneous modification of individual word forms. Furthermore, a demonstration using the social media language variety facilitates accessible annotation of informal, yet comprehensible Arabic.

Researchers have used photochemistry and spectral analysis to investigate temperate terrestrial planets with hydrogen-rich atmospheres, modeled after super-Earth 55 Cancri e. Initially, we determined the photochemical equilibrium of key atmospheric components including hydrogen, hydroxyl, molecular hydrogen, water, methane, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide. We then assessed how these gases influence the planet's temperature and reflectivity across different wavelengths, which we found could help in distinguishing 55 Cancri e from its star using current and upcoming telescopes. However, we also discovered that a thick hydrogen-rich atmosphere would not remain stable under 55 Cancri e's intense stellar radiation, causing it to lose any water present. As a result, we conclude that such an atmosphere is unlikely to exist on this planet.

To differentiate between the Majorana peak and other peaks in tunneling spectra, we suggest utilizing tunneling spectroscopy with linearly damped systems. By replacing superconducting tunnel electrodes with resistive ones, the Bogoliubov-de Gennes spectrum can be described analytically, offering clear separation between various tunneling peaks. Our findings indicate that in a clean spinless quantum point contact, the energy at which the Majorana peak reaches its maximum corresponds to the system's ground state energy. In contrast, for a quantum point contact with impurities, this correlation does not hold.

The advent of Deep Learning in computer vision has led to breakthroughs in automatic flaw detection on road surfaces, paving the way for the development of a comprehensive system that integrates street flaw identification and management. A new platform called RoadAtlas has been launched to accelerate the progress of research in this area by providing access to real-world video footage of highway travel. Located in Ontario, Canada, this digital marketplace provides researchers and educators with easy access to datasets and processing tools for road flaw detection in side-objective detection and continues this pace in image segmentation.

The concept of shadows forms a innovative expansion of traditional bicategorical theory, functioning as a fundamental building block for numerous advanced structures within 2-categorical theory. Specifically, shadows serve an analogous purpose to tracks across various bicategories, demonstrating their versatility through distinct applications such as in the case of bicategories featuring accessible limits or compactifications. Notably, the concept of shadows encompasses multiple variants of double negation operators, each with its own set of limiting properties, and finds a practical application in the decomposition of complex structures like Cauchy completion, Stacks Theorem, and effective epimorphisms, among others.

This study aims to localize sounds within a 2D horizontal plane using binary output at various positions. Initially, traditional techniques like CNNs and GMMs were investigated, but they struggled to meet the challenging one-hot output requirement. Subsequently, an innovative non-neural approach based on the acoustic image concept was proposed and tested. Although the theoretical acoustic image concept has limitations due to real-world absorption effects, it was adapted to solve the localization problem by analyzing frequencies affected by interference patterns, achieving remarkable results even with a single microphone.

This paper presents a new type of graph neural network called Lorentzian Graph Neural Network (LGNN) that is based on a variation of the Hough transform, specifically in the context of relativistic geometry. By leveraging the linear nature of the relational Hough transform, LGNN can naturally incorporate prior knowledge and smoothly integrate features from different representations, such as node and subgraph features, by treating them as different projections of a single feature space.

The problem of a structure interacting with a fluid can be represented as a sequence of nonlinear acoustic contacts, and our work solves the absolute continuity stability reverse problem for this structural engagement. The established continuity stability property allows us to obtain the desired absolute continuity preservation solution to the reverse problem.

In a successful optomechanical circuit transfer, the option exists to operate the system in a steady-state compression mode, yielding a mechanically oriented output with elevated gain. Our analysis of this process in an isolated setup reveals that thermal noise can significantly hinder the production of the compressed state. To overcome this limitation, we propose a method involving the use of an ancillary oscillator to achieve the desired compression transfer in a disconnected system. Notably, this approach exhibits robustness to thermal fluctuations and thermal gain, and can be utilized in isolated systems to directly utilize the compressed mechanical mode through optomechanical interactions.

We examine an expansion of traditional mu-calculus that accommodates scalar, vectorial, and non-deterministic formulas, which determine properties of transition systems that can also be probabilistic. Both the syntax and semantics of this enriched mu-calculus are altered, with semantics offering a more flexible framework for expressing desired properties. A key benefit of this approach is that all desirable properties of the standard mu-calculus remain applicable in its probabilistic variant. Furthermore, we present translation methods to express these formulas in their respective enhanced non-deterministic, probabilistic, and standard mu-calculi.

We present a revised efficient exponential delay discounting model that incorporates a diverse range of human behaviors more effectively than existing theories. This model is based on the efficient variable annuity design and incorporates a dynamic, two-period utility maximization process. By examining how humans discount future outcomes in relation to time, we found that the model's predictions more closely align with empirical data, particularly for discounting future events that are more than one period away. Additionally, the model provides insightful predictions regarding how humans' discounting behavior may be influenced by events in the past or future, potentially offering valuable implications for understanding and treating addiction.

In Substantial Gravity's harmonic coordinate gauges, the condition for the harmonic nature of time requires separating the choice of spatial and temporal gauge functions. This separation enables the derivation of explicit formulas for the spatial gauge functions based on known mass-energy distributions. Notably, specific harmonic gauge conditions can be expressed as wave equations with Gaussian source terms in four-dimensional flat spacetime, allowing for the determination of unique solutions given appropriate boundary conditions at infinity. Furthermore, the concept of harmonic gauge conditions being satisfied within a particular four-dimensional harmonic region can be elaborated upon.

We investigate signed graphs, which are graphs that are assigned the value +1 or -1 on their edges. Notably, the concept of homomorphisms in signed graphs extends that of regular graphs in a natural way. Recent research by Postle and Toh (2021) has established the existence of extended double covers as a graph parameter for some graphs, indicating an infinite sequence of graphs with a specific property where near-maximal connections to another graph with a specific symmetry result in increasingly dense another graph. In this work, we generalize this finding to signed graphs and demonstrate that extended double covers also exist for signed graphs. This discovery has significant implications, allowing us to prove that the set of signed graphs that are planar, have a specific tree-like structure, or are bipartite forms a limit set under the notion of convergent sequences of graphs with a specific boundary property. Additionally, our work provides a more comprehensive understanding of the bipartite graph limit theory developed by Postle and Toh.

A transformation is applied to the Weyy-Wigner representation of canonical thermal equilibrium conditions, which are expressed as operator equations, resulting in a phase-space representation that incorporates the Poincare series expansion of the relevant functions.

The notion of negative absolute temperature, initially proposed by Lambert in 1911 and later developed by Gibbs in 1902, has been relatively little discussed within the context of statistical physics, particularly with respect to the fundamental principles of the subject. We aim to demonstrate that, given the inclusion of two-variable entropy functions, as generally applicable to all systems, the concept of negative temperature arises naturally and, therefore, should no longer be regarded as paradoxical.

Let $A$ and $B$ be non-empty finite subsets of integers. For any integer $c$, the constrained signed sumset $A+B_c$ is defined as the set of all integers that can be represented in the form $a+b'$, where $a$ and $b$ are elements of $A$ and $B$ respectively, and $b'$ equals $b$ or $-b$ such that $b \equiv b' \equiv c \pmod 2$. Building on this definition, we aim to establish Conjectures similar to those of Erdős and Erdős-Gyárfás for sets that satisfy $|A+B_c| \leq |A|+|B|-1$ and $|A+B_c| < |A|+|B|-1$. These new conjectures will then allow us to prove Theorems regarding specific constrained sumsets, including $[m,3m-2]+[m,4m-4]_c$ for integers $m \geq 2$ and $m \geq 3$ respectively, as well as $[m,m^2-2]+[m,3m^2-4m-2]_c$.

Evaluating colorectal polyps via histological analysis from H&E stained tissue samples is a well-established practice.  However, the manual assessment via microscopy can be time-consuming and requires the creation of evaluation tools based on computer-aided diagnosis.  Accurate automated evaluation relies on accurate class labels for automated methods, which are difficult to obtain due to variable expert annotations and the high cost of discarded samples.  In order to support research in this field, we present UniToPatho, an annotated dataset consisting of 4424 images derived from 1134 tissue samples of human colorectal polyps, stained and analyzed for accurate classification and evaluation of polyp areas into four distinct categories.

This research introduces a novel method that utilizes absorbing layers to address scattering problems at high frequencies. The approach employs the time-dependent Maxwell's equations combined with numerical methods based on finite element approximations. A primary challenge with these methods is the development of non-physical numerical artifacts in the form of backward-scattered waves, which can significantly compromise the accuracy of forward-scattered wave simulations. The issues with scattering are mitigated in this study by restricting the range of frequencies for which the method is effective or by reducing the frequency of incoming waves through the narrowing of spectral gaps. The effectiveness of the approach is confirmed by theoretical analysis and practical validation using numerical experiments.

A theory called moist olivine chondritogenesis is proposed to explain the composition of early planetesimals through chemical reactions within water-rich asteroids that were not fully differentiated. These asteroids slowly formed terrestrial planets by accumulating as they did so. Research indicates that water-containing asteroids were water vapor saturated and possessed vapor-filled spaces, supporting the condition necessary for the formation of terrestrial planets in a relatively dry state, even in planets like Venus, which is heavily covered in atmospheric vapor. Computational models demonstrated that dry-ice coated particles with volatile-suppressing effects could accelerate growth in differentiation-less asteroids. Observations of water in the Chelyabinsk and Benenitra meteorites, which originated from the Gravita 3.2-kilometer asteroid, indicate that the asteroid possessed coated particles in a differentiation-less state, providing new evidence for the moist accretion theory. If this theory holds true, a significant portion of planetary water is believed to have been accumulated during the planet formation process.

Using the thermodynamic-limite approach, we calculated the leading asymptotic behavior of the spin-XXZ chain's compact-operator form-factors for all possible helicity configurations, and we expressed these leading terms as simple integrals. Next, we considered a model of higher-spin XXZ chains, and by adapting our integration-method, we derived a set of one-dimensional integrals for the affine-quantine-algebra-symmetric-chain form factors. These integral representations, which are valid for any number-of-spins and for-any-affine-parameters, can also be used to examine-the-convergence-of-the-infinite-series-representations-of-these-form-factors.

Voice translation, specifically cross-language voice translation, allows for translating text to speech in a different language while maintaining the original speaker's language. This paper explores zero-shot voice translation, focusing on generating speech in an unseen language using recording styles from that language and translating those recordings to the target language. Utilizing multi-speaker datasets, the experiment assesses whether models can achieve zero-shot voice translation without fine-tuning or exposure to the target language during training. The study employs a range of metrics to measure metric generation quality, style, and translation accuracy. Furthermore, the results analyze the influence of different dataset sizes and genres.

To compute how light interacts with substances, we first need a way to describe how incoming light carries multi-dimensional spatial information. A method exists to decompose this spatial variability into simpler components, representing it as a sum of orthogonal parts. This approach is used in our research to provide a clear representation of both scattering and optical influence functions. Our research develops a comprehensive framework for 3D electromagnetic systems that extends current methods limited to dipole systems within quantum mechanics. This new method is then applied to create an efficient and user-friendly open-source software tool that generates these functions in a discrete frequency range. The resulting framework enables exact computation of all multipolar systems as demonstrated by our simulated results for a 3D cubic object. The obtained data shows that our method accurately captures the characteristics of various multipolar systems across a wide frequency spectrum.

This study delves into the properties of altered symmetric functions, which were first defined by Schur and later linked to Capelli determinants by Rouby. By integrating ideas from Schur's work on young-bitableaux and Capelli's extended determinants, we establish a connection and provide a joint framework. Specifically, we demonstrate that the altered symmetric functions can be expressed in terms of a new class of multi-linear functions defined on enhanced Young tableaux, which we call the quantum young-bitableaux. Additionally, we identify key relationships between these functions, the altered symmetric functions, and the quantum content character of enhanced Young tableaux, which shed light on the q-deformed Littlewood-Richardson coefficients.

Within the most fundamental scoto-seesaw model, we examine dark matter candidate properties and the consistency of the Standard Model's vacuum, finding limited consistency within a specific range of parameters. Analyzing a set of minimum chromaticity parameters, we determine that dark matter must have a mass between 4.56 times 10^9 GeV and 6.14 times 10^9 GeV for the vacuum to remain stable. These findings highlight the necessity of imposing limits on the stability of the vacuum to fully explore the phenomenology of minimal dark matter models and their connection to neutrino masses.

The concept of bond hybridization, where electron clouds overlap and shape changes occur due to electron-electron interactions, is central to chemistry but challenging to measure through existing techniques. Our group utilized multiple methods, including mass spectrometry and X-ray spectroscopy, along with theoretical models, to demonstrate the significant mixing of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ $d$-orbital sets in various oxides and selenides of multiple 4d and 5d transition metals. Specifically, the degree of blending was found to vary systematically with the relative energy levels of the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals, as indicated by X-ray absorption spectra. The energy differences between these orbital sets can be manipulated by changing the anion, and our observations highlight the significant existence of bond hybridization within the transition metal complex, despite the presence of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ Coulomb repulsion.

In this study, we've expanded the scope of relative quantum $R$-homology for projective varieties within a fixed birational equivalence class. For any such variety $X$ and cycle $\beta$, we've defined relative quantum $R$-homology groups denoted as $HR_{*}(X/Y,\beta)$. These definitions come with a natural multiplication structure, forming a ring known as the relative quantum $R$-cohomology ring, written as $HR_{*}(X/Y)$. Notably, these definitions remain consistent across the varieties in question, yielding an isomorphism in homology between $HR_{*}(X/X_{0},\beta)$ and $HR_{*}(X/Y,\beta)$ for any variety $X_{0}$ that shares the same relationship with $X$ as $X_{0}$ does with $Y$. This equality implies that the relative quantum $R$-homology ring $HR_{*}(X/X_{0})$ is also equivalent to its counterpart $HR_{*}(X/Y)$. Moreover, if $X$ and $Y$ share specific properties (being smooth, toric, or smooth toric), these corresponding relative quantum $R$-homology rings will be isomorphic to their respective absolute counterparts.

Diagnosing patients by analyzing medical images has a long history of success.
This method's accuracy can be improved by using AI to create artificial patient images for practice and training, but currently, there is no clear and systematic approach to producing chest X-rays that accurately represent specific illnesses, leaving this task largely unmet in medical research.
We propose a new, illness-sensitive method for creating modified chest X-rays, allowing practitioners to accurately simulate specific conditions in medical imaging for more effective practice and training.

ViDaExpert is an innovative application that provides robust non-linear visualization and examination capabilities for multidimensional vector data.
This tool is particularly useful in examining complex data sets such as object detections in video footage or spatial data.
By integrating cutting-edge linear and non-linear dimensionality reduction techniques like PCA, UMAP, and t-SNE, ViDaExpert automatically determines the most suitable visualization method for different data sets, ensuring a thorough and efficient examination process.

This paper provides an unbiased estimation of certain Newtonian potentials and their gradients on various convex two-dimensional domains, utilizing random samples. Specifically, we offer fast estimation methods for functions related to Newtonian potentials on flat triangular and quadrangular regions as well as convex polygons made from such triangles and quadrangles. These methods provide not only point-wise values and gradient vectors for the potential functions but also global values when the functions are integrated over a given domain. The underlying implementation is implemented in the R programming language, making it readily accessible for users to utilize.
